note: Rao 2015 truncation ladder; c114 surface-expresses via the membrane-proximal 4H11 epitope. Stays proximal to the AWFPLDSNGTLP Golgi cleavage site so the display does not shed.
One full SEA repeat; carries the canonical CA125/OC125 epitope but sheds it. Use only if that epitope must be displayed.
Niessen 1997 residue-level map; truncate after ~1355 and alpha6beta4 still reaches the surface. Spinardi 1995 (7721947) showed the tail-less form binds laminin.
Harris 2004; expressed alone it is surface-displayed and fully endocytic for hyaluronan. Starts internally, so it needs an exogenous leader.
Gordon 2009 measured surface export of NRR+TM+ICD directly. NRR starts at LNR1; keep it intact or the uncleaved form sheds.
Same minimal design as NOTCH1, measured in the same paper.
Li 2008 surface-expressed leader + NRR + TM in 293T.

Oinuma 2004: TM + full cytoplasmic GAP reaches the membrane. A juxtamembrane stub is kept because a signal peptide butted straight against the TM leaves nothing to cleave and the TM would be read as a signal anchor instead. Constitutively active, so a display chassis rather than ligand-gated. Keep the C-terminal PDZ motif.

Obermoeller-McCormick 2001 mLRP4 = one ligand-binding cluster + TM + tail. Cluster IV is the workhorse; cluster I misfolds. Li 2000 (10747918): keep the YXXL tail motif for endocytosis. May need RAP co-expression.
Takeda 2003 / Marzolo 2003: a one-cluster megalin minireceptor surface-expresses and endocytoses.
Jones 2024 ECD-deleted ROS1 is membrane-expressed. Tends to be constitutively active, so prefer kinase-dead for a display antigen.
Lorente 2005 short RPTP-beta (860 aa deleted from the ECD) surface-expresses in U87.
Bluemel 2010: the membrane-proximal D3 domain carries the most potent engager epitope, and smaller surface antigens engage better.
Andersen 2006 CR-cluster is the minimal APP-binding module; Jacobsen 2001 ectodomain surface-expresses. No published anchored minireceptor, so this combines the two.
Mahnke 2000: TM + tail is endocytic on a heterologous ectodomain. Gully 2020 (33257321): the CTLDs interlock, so keep a contiguous block rather than excising internal ones.

strategy: V-set d1 plus stalk + TM + tail
note: Klaas 2023: fewer than 4 Ig domains loses cell-ligand binding through glycocalyx burial, so keep stalk. Van Breedam 2013: keep the native TM and tail.
No published minimal STAB1. Mirrors the STAB2 HARE design; graft the DDSLL tail motif.

Pinskey 2022 built PLXNA1-dECD and measured surface localisation directly with an extracellular MYC epitope, permeabilised against non-permeabilised. The only dECD plexin with a published surface measurement in its own gene.

Huang 2021 built a human lentiviral PLXNB2 dEcto deleting residues 30-1189, Addgene 86238, and it rescued cell dispersion. That construct leaves only 18 residues of stub, so our 30 is the conservative choice.
No dECD published in A2 itself. Full-length PLXNA2 was expressed and functional in the same paper, vector and assay as the A1 dECD, so the recipe inherits from A1.
Inherits from A1. The apparent red flag that PlexinA3 does not transduce Sema3 is about NRP1 pairing, not trafficking, and is moot once the sema domain is deleted.
Inherits from A1; full-length A4 was functional in the same assay.

strategy: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub, native signal replaced
note: No B3-specific truncation. UniProt flags an erroneous initiation and extended N-terminus for Q9ULL4, and the annotated 44-residue signal has its hydrophobic core well downstream of Met1, so do not trust SIGNAL 1-44 here. Use a heterologous leader or settle the start codon first.
No D1-specific dECD. D-class is neither A nor B, so this is a two-step transfer and the weakest in the family. The best candidate for a hedge arm.
